newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen in 99.80-100.35 range before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen in 99.80-100.35 range before FOMC.

text.p: German Bunds held on to their gains in late trade, shrugging off better-than-expected regional inflation data as the market remained firmly rangebound ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
June Bunds were at 100.08 at 1600 GMT, up 0.13 from Friday's close. They had traded between 99.89 and 100.19 all day and dealers forecast a range of 99.80 to 100.35 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the market had factored in a 25 basis-point rise in U.S. rates and that the impact for Bunds of such a move was unlikely to be great.
"If the FOMC does not raise rates it might even be worse for the market since everyone would be expecting a rate rise next time," one Bund dealer said.

Nevertheless, the FOMC vigil is dominating the market to such an extent that dealers ignored news that consumer prices in the west German state of North Rhine-Westphalia fell 0.2 percent in March, beating forecasts of a rise by 0.1 percent.
In February, the month-on-month rise had been 0.5 percent. The year-on-year inflation rate in March slowed to 1.8 percent in March from 2.0 percent in February.

"North Rhine-Westphalia failed to make a big impression, it's all range trading here," one dealer said. The state's data are the first of four first sets of regional inflation figures from which preliminary west German inflation is calculated.
